Treat adding a normal catalog material as full membership in the canonical block, horizontal slab, stair, wall, Vertical Slab, Step, Layer, Corner, and Quarter Column roles unless an exact technical exclusion is recorded.
Keep canonical material identity separate from geometry generation so limited special forms such as Farmland Slab remain explicitly canonical-bound without implying a full generated family.
Require every BGE-owned registered block to have one explicit canonical classification or a documented exemption, with bootstrap validation preventing anonymous material-semantic holes.

Generate one Layer, Corner, and Quarter Column per supported canonical family while preserving Vertical Slab and Step, deterministic selector order, one-source economy, orientation, waterlogging, collision, and drops.

It adds no name- or provider-specific exclusion, synthetic geometry combination, canonical binding, validation bypass, registration, resource, placement, economy, CTM, or provider-behavior change.

C90 changes only the C87 deferred-CNM-Wall lifecycle after ShapeMap resolves a component: when that resolved component already has a real provider Wall, BGE retires and explicitly exempts its preregistered provisional deferred Wall rather than injecting or binding it; when the component has no real Wall, the same provisional block remains its normal canonical Wall. This is component- and role-based, not a material, namespace, provider, or Enderscape compatibility path; it creates no synthetic binding, does not weaken validation, does not alter C89's non-root guard, and does not change normal CNM family autopopulation, registration, geometry, placement, economy, CTM, resources, or provider behavior.

C93 changes only explicitly cataloged provider-family ownership and the shared rendering contracts requested for Walls, item/selector previews, lowered Path culling and Step UVs, and Corrupt Overgrowth state projection. It records the state/block identity, tint index, quad direction/sprite, selected `BlockTintSource`, and ARGB immediately before vanilla multiplies the quad color, once per block. It does not replace a tint source, cancel rendering, modify a quad, or use a spruce name/ID heuristic; native spruce, birch fixed tint, ordinary biome foliage, all geometry, UVs, placement, family membership, ShapeMap ordering, drops, economy, CTM, and C96's tinted-Stair correction remain unchanged.
Clutter No More source and artifacts remain external and unchanged; its ShapeMap remains the canonical family and switching mechanism.

C68 changes only normal axis-material Layer face UV rectangles: it preserves Layer bounds, placement, collision, state, texture roles, grain rotation, special visual paths, non-axis materials, all other geometries, registration, data, display transforms, and external-material support.
`projects/bge-ctm`, shaders, resource-pack classification, BBB source/assets, and unrelated consumer projects are outside this consolidation.

C84 corrects the Blistered Magnia `ofFullCopy` state-callback seam through an explicit Enderscape material-state bridge: geometry state remains separate while Nebulite power, Magnia power, Blistered Magnia polarity, and Blinklamp luminance are carried into every derived role. BBB source bytes, derivative texture bytes, and the resulting JAR are PRIVATE_LOCAL_ONLY: no such bytes may be tracked, distributed, released, uploaded, or placed in public resource paths; build output and ignored local artifact retention are the sole authorized storage. state.milestone: C97 is a diagnostic successor to exact C96 `BGE C96.jar`, SHA-256 `4f8ea46d2766bab183a958790ea6c696621cb9dbdec4b11bdf9ae878cfecedf7`: the owner observed those exact bytes still gave derived spruce geometry biome-dependent visible foliage color instead of native spruce's fixed color. Read-only local auditing found resource-pack mechanisms that can affect models, tags, or colors, and local shader material classification that names native but not BGE leaves; it did not establish active pack order or a runtime renderer/shader cause. C97 consequently makes no speculative override. It logs both native and exact-family derived tint inputs at `ModelBlockRenderer.putQuadWithTint`, immediately before the Java renderer multiplies the quad ARGB, so the first divergence can be observed under the actual stack. Java 25 controlled validation passed all 165/165 GameTests, the isolated client lookup regression, and the new required renderer-mixin load; C97 remains ACTIVE and runtime-untested. Accepted C70 and rollback C72 are unchanged.

exceptions.reason: The exact C97 artifact targets the Minecraft 26.2 release and packages Fabric's same-release predicate; because it contains privately derived BBB Beam resources, this target-specific artifact is PRIVATE_LOCAL_ONLY and has no redistribution permission.
regression_evidence: Java 25 clean packaging produced exact PRIVATE_LOCAL_ONLY `BGE C97.jar`, 6,426,611 bytes, SHA-256 3e13d6f4dfe46edea753926da4e1168515e8432dce85d63a29b360a6aefc9408, finalized at 2026-09-22T15:09:08.6623340Z from preceding coherent C96 checkpoint 0b047026a4e3e7539cbf2ef69a176d9292147aee.

The private Beam generator accepted only locally supplied BBB dev.6 SHA-256 0d54034725c3e354515c78bcee32ab2cb5ce764a33e0602419e26c78aaef8c5a and Enderscape 3.0.2+mc26.2 SHA-256 9fcc4f59ca88e91f90e7c7d18289f2f859f20c810eebcca924764aa15236c40b; verification found six approved private Beam PNGs, zero provider-resource entries, and zero forbidden source-artwork leakage.

The read-only audit covered every immediate `originals/resourcepacks` item. `Chat Reporting Helper`, `Enhanced Audio r7`, `FreshAnimations_v1.10.5`, `inventory-particles-matcha-compat-c3`, `Matcha GUI Compat v4`, `Mizuno_Fresh_Animations_Condensed_26.2`, `Neutral Sea Grass and Kelp`, `Ribbit Villagers v4 - florist routing fix`, and `Serified Font v1.2` contained no block-color, colormap, CTM, BGE-spruce, model-tint, tag/classification, or shader mechanism. FreshAnimations, Mizuno, and Ribbit contain only OptiFine CEM entity resources in the relevant namespace.

`Foundation v2` has `polytone/biome_modifiers/lush_caves.json` with only `grass_color`, vine-only OptiFine CTM, and a native `minecraft:spruce_leaves` random bushy-model replacement whose template-leaves faces retain tint semantics; `Matcha_Flavoured_1_12` replaces native spruce-leaf models/textures and ships vanilla foliage/grass colormaps but has no OptiFine, Polytone, Colormatic, CTM, or BGE/CNM target; `Matcha-Overlays-v37` has a spruce-log-only OptiFine overlay (including `tintIndex=0`/`tintBlock=spruce_log`) and nine BGE bookshelf-only model references, not spruce geometry. Foundation and Matcha Flavoured both replace native spruce assets, so their active pack order would determine their native-resource precedence; that unavailable order was not invented.

The local `clutternomore` pack has no OptiFine/MCPatcher, Polytone, Colormatic, CTM, custom-color, or shader metadata. Its BGE leaf models use tint index 0 and its `data/minecraft/tags/block/leaves.json` classifies the three BGE spruce Layer/Corner/Quarter Column IDs as leaves, which is a potential downstream classification input but not itself a color provider. No audited pack directly targets BGE spruce geometry. No locally supplied Continuity, Sodium, Iris, Indium, Polytone, or Colormatic JAR was available to inspect; that does not claim such components are absent from an uninspected profile.

Source inspection establishes the Java seam: Minecraft 26.2 `ModelBlockRenderer.putQuadWithTint` obtains the quad tint index, resolves `BlockColors`/`BlockTintSource.colorInWorld`, then calls `QuadInstance.multiplyColor` before output. CNM 2.0.7's HEAD-cancellable `BlockColors.getTintSources` mixin can delegate ShapeMap children to a parent; C96's priority-900 interception replaces only the frozen exact eight before that delegation. Complementary Unbound r5.8.1 locally classifies native `spruce_leaves` in `block.properties` as leaves but names no BGE IDs; its leaves material code operates on already-submitted color. That is a plausible post-Java classification difference, not runtime proof.

The C97 controlled Minecraft 26.2 suite passed 165/165 GameTests. The isolated client fixture retained `SPRUCE_FINAL_TINT_LOOKUP|targets=8|contexts=2|canonicalControls=2|result=PASS`, and the required C97 `ModelBlockRenderer.putQuadWithTint` mixin loaded in that client run; the fixture does not render world quads and therefore produced no actual-stack trace line or runtime conclusion. The material/profile architecture suite (including the C97 no-override seam check), the 11-check Glass Corner UV audit, and unified artifact verification passed while retaining all C96 stair-frame and unrelated BGE coverage.

C97 logs one `BGE_SPRUCE_TINT_TRACE` row per rendered native/derived block immediately before Java color multiplication. Until actual-stack rows are supplied, the last observed equivalence and first visible divergence remain unproven; C97 has no gameplay runtime result or acceptance. It retains C94 item presentation, C93 provider-role completion, C96 tinted-Stair frames, every prior foliage contract, and all non-tint BGE behavior.
